report_name: Optimizely Supply-Chain Attack Injects Malicious Code into 178 Major Websites

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
attack_patterns.description: Attackers compromised the Optimizely web experimentation platform, a third-party software service, to inject malicious JavaScript into the websites of its customers.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: The attack abused the functionality of the Optimizely web experimentation platform to inject malicious scripts into customer projects, leveraging it as a public-facing application.

attack_patterns.name: Drive-by Compromise
attack_patterns.description: Visitors to the compromised websites had their browsers load and execute the malicious JavaScript payload served from an attacker-controlled domain.

attack_patterns.name: JavaScript
attack_patterns.description: The malicious payload was written in JavaScript and executed within the victim's browser to perform its functions, including data skimming and crypto clipping.

attack_patterns.name: Credentials from Web Browsers
attack_patterns.description: The malware acted as a web skimmer to capture credit card details from payment forms and also stole cookies.

attack_patterns.name: Transmitted Data Manipulation
attack_patterns.description: The malware functioned as a crypto clipper, replacing cryptocurrency wallet addresses on webpages and in the user's clipboard with attacker-controlled addresses.

attack_patterns.name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
attack_patterns.description: The initial script loader injected into Optimizely snippets was obfuscated using Base64 encoding to evade detection.

malware.name: Optimizely Supply-Chain Malware
malware.description: A multi-purpose JavaScript malware injected via the Optimizely platform, designed to skim payment card details, hijack cryptocurrency transactions, and deliver exploits.

malware.name: Coruna
malware.description: An exploit kit delivered by the Optimizely supply-chain malware, targeting vulnerabilities in older, unpatched versions of iOS and iPadOS.

malware.name: DarkSword
malware.description: An exploit kit delivered by the Optimizely supply-chain malware, targeting vulnerabilities in older, unpatched versions of iOS and iPadOS.

tools.name: Optimizely
tools.description: Legitimate web experimentation platform that was compromised by attackers and used as a vector to inject malicious JavaScript into customer websites.

identities.name: BBC
identities.description: One of the major media organizations whose website was compromised to serve malicious JavaScript via the Optimizely platform.

identities.name: CNN
identities.description: One of the major media organizations whose website was compromised to serve malicious JavaScript via the Optimizely platform.

identities.name: Zoom
identities.description: One of the major technology companies whose website was compromised to serve malicious JavaScript via the Optimizely platform.

identities.name: Salesforce
identities.description: One of the major technology companies whose website was compromised to serve malicious JavaScript via the Optimizely platform.

identities.name: Equifax
identities.description: One of the affected organizations that had to temporarily disable Optimizely scripts to mitigate the supply-chain attack.

infrastructure.name: Malicious Payload Server
infrastructure.description: Attacker-controlled server at 1688360.cc used to host the main malicious JavaScript payload (track.js).

infrastructure.name: Compromised Optimizely CDN
infrastructure.description: The legitimate Optimizely CDN (cdn.optimizely.com) that was abused to serve the initial malicious script loader to visitors of compromised websites.

indicators.name: Optimizely Supply-Chain Attack C2 Domain
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Optimizely Supply-Chain Attack C2 DNS Query
id: 2b1a8c3d-f4e5-4b9a-8c7d-6e5f4d3c2b1a
status: experimental
description: Detects DNS queries to a C2 domain associated with the Optimizely supply-chain attack.
references:
  - https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2026/11/cnn-bbc-zoom-and-other-sites-served-malicious-code-in-supply-chain-attack
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-17
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.command_and_control
level: high
logsource:
  category: dns_query
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName: '1688360.cc'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects DNS queries to the known malicious domain 1688360.cc used in the Optimizely supply-chain attack.

indicators.name: Optimizely Supply-Chain Attack Payload URL
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Optimizely Supply-Chain Attack Payload URL Access
id: 9d8c7b6a-5f4e-4d3c-2b1a-8c7d6e5f4d3c
status: experimental
description: Detects web requests for a malicious JavaScript payload associated with the Optimizely supply-chain attack.
references:
  - https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2026/11/cnn-bbc-zoom-and-other-sites-served-malicious-code-in-supply-chain-attack
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-17
tags:
  - attack.t1189
  - attack.initial_access
level: high
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    c-uri|contains: '1688360.cc/track.js'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects web requests to the malicious URL hosting the track.js payload.

indicators.name: Suspicious JavaScript Filename track.js
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious JavaScript Filename track.js
id: 1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a9b-8c7d-6e5f4d3c2b1a
status: experimental
description: Detects web requests for a file named 'track.js', which was used as a payload in the Optimizely supply-chain attack. This may have false positives.
references:
  - https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2026/11/cnn-bbc-zoom-and-other-sites-served-malicious-code-in-supply-chain-attack
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-17
tags:
  - attack.t1189
  - attack.initial_access
level: medium
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    c-uri|endswith: '/track.js'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects web requests for a file named 'track.js', which was the name of the malicious payload in the Optimizely attack.

indicators.name: Potential Obfuscated Payload Execution via Base64
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Obfuscated Payload Execution via Base64
id: 8c7d6e5f-4d3c-4b1a-9d8c-7b6a5f4e3d2c
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of 'base64 -d' which may indicate decoding of a malicious payload, as seen in the Optimizely supply-chain attack.
references:
  - https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2026/11/cnn-bbc-zoom-and-other-sites-served-malicious-code-in-supply-chain-attack
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-17
tags:
  - attack.t1140
  - attack.defense_evasion
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '/base64'
    CommandLine|contains: ' -d'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of 'base64 -d' command, which could be used to decode obfuscated payloads as described in the attack.
